small screens are not a panacea for digital library delivery and there are many challenges to be overcome in order to deliver a satisfactory user experience

small-screen digital library access has the potential to be very useful in many situations; small-screen DL access is not yet widely used, and the DL community has not yet fully considered the implications of such access for their DL systems; and, the Greenstone DL system has been used successfully to deliver DL access via small-screen devices.
small-screen DL access is feasible, but there are many issues to consider.

the use of small-screen DL systems, and we believe that the issues presented here are of interest to DL researchers.
the use of DL systems in small screen environments, and the impact of this use on the DL community.
how to provide small screen access to digital library content, and the issues and concerns which arise when doing this.

small screen access is a complex and multi-faceted issue.
small-screen access is a significant challenge for digital libraries.
small-screen access is not currently feasible, but that the potential for it in the future is very exciting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
small-screen access is a valuable addition to the range of services which a DL can provide.
small screen devices have a place in the Digital Library landscape.
small screens are an important access channel for digital library content, and the community should consider them in their designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
small screen devices have become ubiquitous, and DLs need to take this into account.
small-screen access is not simply a matter of reducing screen size, it also involves a number of other considerations which are not always obvious.

the DL community needs to be aware of the issues involved in delivering small-screen access, and to be aware that the small screen is not just an alternative to the larger display, but is also an important access point in its own right.
